title: Open model matchmaking — catalog walkthrough & compat grid
next_steps: Redwood to share model-compatibility spreadsheet and perf benchmarks by 2025-11-10
Customer to send sample workload + S3 access for staging tests by 2025-11-14
Schedule Dedicated capacity pricing follow-up with finance (tentative 2025-11-17)
action_items: Alex Chen: Share compatibility matrix CSV and perf slides — due 2025-11-10
Maya O'Connor: Provide sample prompt set and dataset access — due 2025-11-14
Priya Singh: Prepare quick benchmarking run with quantized L7 model — due 2025-11-13
header: 2025-11-07 09:00 PST / 16:00 UTC — Duration 58m. Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (DataThrive Head of Platform), Maya O'Connor (ML Engineer), Samir Patel (Infra Lead)
summary: Product walkthrough focused on Redwood's model catalog, how to select open models, interpret benchmark results, and use the compatibility matrix. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, quantization/latency, VPC requirements, and next steps to run a short benchmark with DataThrive's sample workload.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time this morning. Quick roll call — Alex Chen here on the AE side, Priya Singh is my SE. Jordan, Maya, Samir from DataThrive?
[00:12] Jordan: Yep, Jordan here. Morning. Maya and Samir on as well.
[00:16] Maya: Morning all.
[00:18] Samir: Morning.
[00:20] Alex: Cool. Goal for today: run through the model catalog live, show how you can pick open models, read the perf bench numbers, and use the compat grid so you know what runs where — and then plan a short benchmark with your prompts. Sound right?
[00:32] Jordan: That's perfect. We're mainly trying to figure out which open models give us the best latency/cost tradeoff for our realtime summarization endpoints.
[00:38] Priya: Got it. Real-time summarization, can you remind us of target p95 latency and throughput? And what infra you plan to run in — hosted, dedicated, or private VPC?
[00:48] Jordan: Target p95 under 250ms on short requests, about 10 rps steady per instance. We prefer VPC for data controls but flexible on Dedicated if pricing is workable.
[00:59] Alex: Okay, makes sense. We'll demo both hosted and a dedicated pattern — show how the compat matrix flags models that are friendly to quantization and where the KV cache helps.
[01:10] [01:10] Priya: Opening the catalog — quick note, some of the auto-transcribed names in the UI are slightly different in the feed, so I'll call out the exact model slugs as we go. I clicked the "Open models" filter and applied sequence length of 512 and cost sensitivity "moderate".
[01:28] Maya: Sorry, can you slow on the filter steps? We're screen-sharing as well.
[01:33] Priya: Sure. Filter: license=open, sequence<=512, token-cost bucket = moderate. Results: Llama-compat-7B-8k-quant, Red7L-quant (note: internal alias), and a couple of bloom-family variants. Each row shows throughput on A100, H100, and T4 — plus an estimated per-token cost.
[01:52] Jordan: That per-token cost — what assumptions drive it? Is it batch size, KV hits, or just raw hardware time?
[01:58] Alex: Good question. The cost is modeled from throughput at the median sequence length you pick: it assumes default batching (continuous batching profile), KV cache hit rate of 0% unless you enable prefix caching, and average token length equal to the sequence filter. We show alternative scenarios in the Optimize tab.
[02:17] [02:17] Priya: I'm opening the benchmark details for Red7L-quant: p50 token latency 6ms on H100, p95 single-request latency 240ms for 512 tokens on A100, but shows significant improvement with quant-8 kernel. Also note the compat grid marks it as "quant-friendly" and "KV-safe".
[02:39] Maya: When you say "KV-safe" do you mean the model's KV cache is stable across quantized weights? We've had cache corruption issues with some off-the-shelf runs.
[02:49] Priya: Yeah, it's a shorthand — it means our runtime and kernel selection preserve KV alignment for that quant profile across the set of tested sequence lengths. Not a guarantee but empirically stable in our tests. There's a footnote about "edge cases with cross-attention rewrites" — the transcript may show that as "cross section rewrites" earlier in some autocaptions.
[03:07] Samir: Can you show the comparatives between hosted and dedicated latency for the same model? We need to see tail differences.
[03:13] Alex: On the console I can toggle the deployment target. For the same model and workload, hosted multi-tenant shows slightly higher p95 — we cite about +20-30% overhead due to co-tenancy and routing buffers. Dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs drops that. I'll pull up a sample chart.
[03:30] [03:30] Priya: Chart: p95 vs throughput — hosted line (blue), dedicated (green). At 10 rps steady the p95 for Red7L-quant is ~230ms on dedicated H100 config vs ~290ms hosted.
[03:42] Jordan: That's helpful. What about cold-starts when KV is empty? Our traffic can be bursty and we can't warm everything.
[03:50] Priya: We measure cold-starts in the bench table — first-token latency is higher, but continuous batching and prefix caching drop subsequent tokens quickly. Optimize suggests a tiny cache-warm strategy: keep a small pool of warm replicas or use autoscale buffer for bursts.
[04:04] [04:04] Maya: Any notes on quantization quality? We've seen sometimes the quant-8 step introduces hallucination frequency increases for summarization.
[04:12] Alex: Yes — tradeoff. In Optimize there are quality delta metrics against a float baseline using your prompt set or our reference evals. For summarization tasks we usually suggest running a small eval (50-100 prompts) to check ROUGE/BLEU or human pass/fail. We'll include the quality deltas in the compatibility sheet.
[04:29] Priya: Also, the Console has a "regression alert" toggle so if quality metrics fall below a threshold after a model swap, you get notified and can auto-roll back.
[04:38] [04:38] Jordan: Nice. On security, can we get an architecture note for VPC private control plane? We need KMS integration and audit logs for SOC2.
[04:47] Alex: Absolutely. We have a Private deployment option with customer-managed VPC, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs retained per the enterprise plan. I'll share the security pack link after the call (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack — note: placeholder in the transcript). We'll also include SOC2 attestations.
[05:03] Samir: About model variants and routing — can we automatically fallback to a cheaper model if the primary is saturated? Our budget is strict.
[05:12] Priya: Yes, routing policies can be configured per-route: prefer low-latency model, fallback to cost-optimized variant, or region-based routing. There's also automatic degradation to quantized variant if the float variant hits capacity.
[05:26] [05:26] Maya: Can you show the compatibility matrix file format? We prefer CSV so DEVOPS can ingest it into our infra tooling.
[05:33] Priya: The compat grid exports as CSV with columns: model_slug, license, recommended_quant_profile, compatible_kernels, supported_sequence_lengths, preferred_hardware, expected_p95_ms@seq_len, quality_delta_vs_float, notes. I'll export live.
[05:45] [05:45] Alex: Export done — I'm dropping a link in the chat (link: https://files.redwood.example/export/compat-grid-ff-20251107.csv). Please note links in this transcript are smeared by auto-caption sometimes.
[05:58] Jordan: Received. Good. For the benchmarking numbers — do you offer to run a bench for us with our prompts or do we need to run the harness?
[06:06] Priya: We can do either. For a fast turnaround we'll run an initial bench in our sandbox if you provide sample prompts and S3 read access. For production-level numbers we recommend you run the harness in your VPC or dedicated cluster — we'll supply a benchmark template you can run locally.
[06:23] Maya: We can provide a 200-prompt set, should that be fine for a first pass?
[06:27] Alex: Yes, that should be enough to see quality deltas and latency distribution. Aim for representative prompts: short facts, medium-length context, and a few long ones to hit edge cases.
[06:39] [06:39] Samir: Any caveats on the reported per-token cost vs actual cloud egress/managed infra fees?
[06:45] Priya: Our per-token model cost excludes cloud egress and provisioning overheads; dedicated pricing quote will include reserved GPU cost and management fee. We'll send a sample pricing sheet.
[06:55] Jordan: Great.
[06:58] [06:58] Priya: I'm switching to the Optimize tab to show example configuration suggestions. This is where the platform suggests batching levels, quant profiles, and whether a KV cache yields ROI for your workload. The suggestion engine uses your target latency and cost sensitivity.
[07:18] Maya: What's the logic for batching? We don't want to increase tail latency.
[07:23] Priya: Batching is workload-aware. The Optimize engine recommends a batch size that maximizes throughput subject to your p95 SLO. It simulates latency percentiles using a trace of inter-arrival times you can upload.
[07:37] Alex: Quick aside — note that the auto-transcription sometimes writes "K V case" or "K V cache" incorrectly, so reading the record you'll see typos.
[07:45] [07:45] Jordan: Haha yeah already saw a few.
[07:48] Priya: Back to quantization: the compat CSV flags recommended quant kernels — e.g., int8-llm-kernel-v2 or q4_0 etc., and preferred hardware. For example, Red7L-quant prefers H100 with int8 kernel for best latency/cost.
[08:05] Samir: Do you support FP16 fallback in runtime if quantized kernel throws numerical issues?
[08:10] Priya: Yes, our runtime can fallback to a compatible kernel or float profile if numerical instability is detected in runtime checks. There's an operational alert when that happens.
[08:20] [08:20] Maya: Any runbooks you share for regression troubleshooting?
[08:24] Alex: We'll include runbooks in the deck and the security pack. Also in the Console there's a debug-trace link attached to each request so you can inspect token-level timing.
[08:36] Priya: Moving to the compat examples, here's a row for bloom-7b-compat: notes say "not quant-stable" and "T4 slow at long seqs". The grid allows you to filter by "quant-friendly" and show only models recommended for 512 tokens or less.
[08:54] Jordan: How do you validate the quality deltas? Are they automatic or human scored?
[08:59] Priya: By default we run automatic metrics (ROUGE / BLEU / embedding-similarity) and show deltas. For production we recommend paired human evaluation or a small human-in-the-loop sampling — we can help set that up.
[09:12] [09:12] Maya: If we want to run an in-VPC Dedicated trial, what's the lead time and minimum commit?
[09:19] Alex: Typical lead time for Dedicated is 2–4 weeks to provision and test; minimums vary by region and GPU mix. I'll pass you the Dedicated pricing sheet; it's also in the next_steps.
[09:30] Samir: For the bench run you said you'd run an initial sandbox test — does that require us to share data?
[09:36] Priya: We only need obfuscated prompts or a sample prompt set plus S3 read access for benchmarking artifacts. You can redact PII. For any real data we'd recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC.
[09:48] [09:48] Jordan: Okay we can prepare a 200-prompt set and provide a staging S3 link.
[09:52] Alex: Great. I'll follow up with the compatibility CSV and perf slides. Priya will run the initial bench and loop in BenchOps.
[10:02] [10:02] Maya: On routing — can the fallback trigger be based on queue wait time rather than model capacity?
[10:09] Priya: Yes, routing rules can be based on latency thresholds, queue depth, model health, region, or cost windows. It's very flexible.
[10:18] Samir: Any known incompatibilities with our infra stack — we run k8s with Cilium and use strict egress policies.
[10:25] Alex: For Private deployment we support distroless images and can work with Cilium policies. We'll validate in a short onboarding checklist. There may be a few ports and firewall rules to allow tracing; we'll send that checklist.
[10:39] [10:39] Priya: I'm going to show the "compat notes" column — sometimes we put small comments like "repro with 1% tokenization mismatch" or "requires attention at seq>4k".
[10:49] Jordan: Are model cards editable? We want to add an internal note for compliance reasons.
[10:54] Priya: You can attach internal notes to models in your account. Those don't leave the tenant.
[10:58] [10:58] Maya: Any limits to the number of model variants we can pin per route?
[11:03] Alex: No hard limits, but we recommend keeping it to 2–3 variants to keep routing predictable. The console shows a priority order and weight for A/Bing.
[11:13] [11:13] Samir: Ok thanks. A couple of quick technical deep-dive items: memory usage for 512 tokens and KV cache sizing recommendations.
[11:20] Priya: Memory numbers are in the bench table: for Red7L-quant at 512 tokens, KV + activations is ~18GB on H100 with quantized kernels; float is closer to 32GB. We usually recommend reserving 25–30% headroom for KV and beam adjustments.
[11:36] Jordan: That helps.
[11:39] [11:39] Alex: Time check — we're at ~11 minutes into the call; still plenty of time to kick the bench and export artifacts. Anything else high-level?
[11:47] Maya: One more — do you publish your full kernel compat list by model publicly or only to customers?
[11:52] Priya: We publish a public catalog with high-level compat, but the detailed kernel list and perf artifacts are available to customers in the Console/export.
[11:59] [11:59] Jordan: Fine. Let's move to the demo of the actual export rows — show the CSV row for Red7L-quant.
[12:06] Priya: CSV row: "red7l-quant,MIT,int8-llm-kernel-v2;q4_0,H100;A100,seq<=2048,expected_p95=240,quality_delta=-0.8%,notes=quant-friendly". Again the CSV will be dumped to your account.
[12:29] Samir: Nice. For auditing we need request-level logs for 90 days — is that possible?
[12:34] Alex: Yes, audit logs are configurable; enterprise retention options go up to a year. We'll include the audit log retention options in the security pack.
[12:44] [12:44] Maya: Can we map the bench numbers back to a cost model for our finance team? They want an expected cost per 1M tokens for a given model mix.
[12:52] Priya: We have a "cost estimator" tool in Optimize: you give it traffic profile and model mix and it outputs rough cost per token and monthly run-rate. We'll include a canned estimate in the follow-up.
[13:04] Jordan: Anything about model licensing we should be aware of when selecting open models?
[13:10] Alex: The catalog surfaces license terms — MIT vs Apache vs more restrictive. If you plan to fine-tune or redistribute, double-check license and we'll flag anything requiring legal review.
[13:22] [13:22] Maya: ok thanks.
[13:24] Priya: Zooming to the tracks where we show "compatibility score" — it's a heuristic combining quality delta, latency, quant stability, and license friendliness. It helps shortlisting.
[13:36] Jordan: Are these scores tunable per customer? We might weigh quality higher than cost.
[13:41] Priya: Yes — in the Console you can set weighting preferences and the catalog re-sorts.
[13:47] [13:47] Samir: Any gotchas with tokenizer mismatch? We use a custom tokenizer for some clients.
[13:55] Alex: If you use a custom tokenizer the best path is to run the bench harness inside your environment. Tokenization differences can shift cost and quality numbers significantly.
[14:06] [14:06] Maya: Can the Console show token breakdown by prompt vs completion? We want to attribute cost.
[14:11] Priya: Yes, per-request token breakdown and per-route token billing are visible in the billing dashboard.
[14:21] Jordan: Ok timeline wise — we'll prepare the 200-prompt set and S3 by 11/14. What's the expected turnaround for the initial bench?
[14:29] Alex: If you deliver by 11/14, Priya and BenchOps can run an initial bench and share results by 11/17.
[14:36] [14:36] Samir: That aligns with our internal timeline.
[14:39] Priya: Before we wrap — any preference for the bench target config? We'll test Red7L-quant, bloom-7b-compat, and a float baseline.
[14:49] Maya: That seems reasonable.
[14:51] Alex: Great. I'm going to summarize next steps and drop the export and security links. Summary: Redwood to share compat CSV and perf slides (Alex), Priya to run bench with provided prompts (Priya), DataThrive to provide S3 link and prompt set (Maya). We'll schedule a follow-up pricing/delegate call for Dedicated.
[15:13] [15:13] Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks for the walkthrough.
[15:16] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[15:19] Samir: Thanks.
[15:21] Alex: End recap: I'll email the links and a one-page decision matrix for the model shortlist. Bye all.
[15:27] [15:27] -- Meeting ended --

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cache" as "K V case", "quant-8" as "quant ate") and placeholder links used in demo. Shared artifacts: compat CSV (https://files.redwood.example/export/compat-grid-ff-20251107.csv), security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security-pack), perf slides (shared post-call).
